assertions.claim: In global Fibonacci Nim with first bound r = 1, the position with three heaps of size 6 is a P-position (the player to move loses): Outcome <6,6,6,1> false
In global Fibonacci Nim with first bound r = 1, the position with one heap of size 6 (heap sizes 0,0,6) is an N-position (the player to move wins): Outcome <0,0,6,1> true
In global Fibonacci Nim with first bound r = 1, the position with three heaps of size 20 is an N-position: Outcome <20,20,20,1> true
In global Fibonacci Nim with first bound r = 1, the position with one heap of size 20 (heap sizes 0,0,20) is a P-position: Outcome <0,0,20,1> false

reading_of_Outcome: Outcome p true means p is an N-position and Outcome p false means p is a P-position, under the normal-play rule of Model.lean (a move removes t counters, 1 <= t <= min(heap, r), from one heap and the next bound is 2t). That the inductively defined Outcome predicate equals this game-theoretic outcome is a written argument (FORMAL/provenance/MODEL_AND_CORRESPONDENCE_NOTE.md, section Explicit strategy derivations) that a separate reviewer checked; it is not a Lean theorem.
not_covered: the generic equivalence of the inductive Outcome predicate with the game-theoretic outcome (written argument only)
